interpretation: Mechanical grouping of retained open implementation verdicts. No verdict changes or later-acceptance reconciliation. Primary functional placements do not assign common-engine versus source-extension architecture. Secondary dependencies are reported separately and never counted as additional rows. Input provenance is identified by path, assessment cutoff and SHA-256; no repository revision is inferred from an arbitrary input file.

rows.currentReason: The add-on library lists installed and Quaddicted catalog packages and offers install, update, remove and play, with status and error feedback.

rows.currentReason: Demo-product restriction is applied: demo mount restriction, fs_restrict, demoRestricted in server and client admission, and a demo sv_keywords entry.

rows.currentReason: normalizeQ3Bsp converts IBSP44 maps to the version-46 layout before parsing and classifyBsp accepts versions 44 and 46; tests cover IBSP44 decoding and hostile-input rejection.

rows.title: Arena and bot catalogs
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Bot catalog loading is joined, but the tier-classified arena selection and authored-opponent launch workflow is not implemented in the common frontend.

classification.note: Arena/bot catalog discovery supports progression but is a content inventory behavior.

rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q1 addon fog events are emitted as q1-composition events but have no application fog consumer; complete server/map fog transitions therefore remain missing.

rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q1 native presentation projection does not publish raw actor alpha/scale, and complete Q1 shadow/rerelease effect-bit consumers are not joined; particles and beams alone do not complete this row.
rows.currentReason: The Q1 presentation projection publishes raw actor alpha and scale (with clamping), the scene applies them and shadow casting, and the effect-bit consumers (trails, dlights, particles) are joined.

rows.title: Video modes, resize, fullscreen and renderer restart
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Startup renderer/gamma/resolution choices exist, but changing/restarting the renderer in a live session while retaining input/state is not implemented as a complete application workflow.
rows.currentReason: vid_restart [cpu|gl] restarts the renderer between source frames on the retained client and republishes the window to input, with rollback on failure.

rows.title: Restart or switch renderer within a live session
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Startup can recreate display and in-game resizing is supported, but live-session CPU/GL renderer switching with complete world/input/HUD rebuild is not provided.
rows.currentReason: vid_restart [cpu|gl] and the Apply renderer setting switch the renderer in a live session through ApplicationVideoRestart, which republishes the window and rebuilds presentation.

rows.title: Toggle the rerelease flashlight under every host profile
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Rerelease player state emits/restores flashlight events, but no application event consumer produces the requested flashlight light/sound.
rows.currentReason: Flashlight events are consumed by the effects layer, which keeps a per-actor flashlight scene light; toggling in the rerelease module also plays the on/off sounds.

rows.title: Materials and complete CPU/GL rendering
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: CPU/GL implement ordinary animated stages, deformation, fog, sky, portals, lighting, shadows and particles. The compound authored-material requirement is incomplete because the actual application shader registry supplies no cinematic provider, so videoMap material stages remain unresolved.
rows.currentReason: The application shader registry supplies a materialMovie provider that resolves videoMap stages through MaterialCinematic, with fallback when the movie is absent; the rest of the CPU/GL material pipeline was already listed as implemented.

rows.title: Visual settings, display lifecycle and source hardware profiles
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Common graphics options exist, but the complete source hardware-profile/renderer-thread and live restart lifecycle is not joined; Q3 client presentation still receives a generic hardware profile.
rows.currentReason: vid_restart is registered by ApplicationVideoRestart with cpu/gl backend switch and r_smp worker option, and the Q3 client derives its hardware class from the live renderer string via the five-class q3Hardware classifier (only ragepro vs generic reaches effects).

rows.currentReason: The CIN soundtrack is decoded with the video, queued on the cinematic's own mixer lane and paused, checkpointed and resumed with the picture clock; tests assert PCM output and pause behaviour.

rows.currentReason: Music pause and resume run through the cd pause and cd resume commands and source pause events, and music gain is a continuous setter; a startup test checks pause, resume and gain preservation.

rows.title: Background intro/loop music and continuous gain
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Actual world/cgame music supports intro/loop, pause, gain and replacement, but the specified menu/postgame music transitions are not joined with those missing product flows.

rows.title: Archived cvars, bindings and startup configuration

rows.title: NetQuake protocols 15, 666 and 999

rows.currentReason: The Q3 remote client consumes network snapshots and owns presentation prediction with capture on snapshot and map restart.

rows.title: Player names, colors and setup

rows.currentReason: Q1 pause, status, ping and kick are registered and handled with operator feedback; pause is authorized by pausable and the requesting origin.

rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Native Q1 application networking lacks the full player/spectator/password/rcon/IP-filter/flood-protection operator workflow.

classification.note: Admission wire behavior and operator policy share one row; assigned to administration.

rows.currentReason: QW hosting enforces player and spectator passwords, maxspectators, rcon, IP filter commands (addip, removeip, listip) and chat flood protection; NQ hosts apply the IP reject filter.

rows.title: Direct connect, LAN search and server browser
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Direct NQ transport is connected, but complete LAN/master discovery and a usable server-browser workflow are not application features.
rows.currentReason: The startup server browser supports direct connect, LAN broadcast search for NQ and QW, HTTP master lists, filters, sorting and a details view.

rows.title: Configure masters and heartbeat publication
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The live Q2 server adapter does not schedule master registration/heartbeat publication or expose master configuration.
rows.currentReason: The Q2 server adapter sends master heartbeats on a schedule and at shutdown to masters from the administration owner, which also exposes master configuration.

rows.title: Configure player names, skins, handedness, and view settings
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source userinfo parsing and remote updates exist, but local per-participant name/skin/hand/FOV configuration is not fully bound to active application settings.
rows.currentReason: Per-seat name, skin, hand and fov cvars are registered as userinfo, exposed in the settings menu, and changes are published to the running simulation or native guest each frame.

rows.title: Enter spectator mode and chase active players
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source chase movement and target selection run, but primaryUi reads the spectator own combat/inventory rather than the chased player; required borrowed HUD statistics are not joined.
rows.currentReason: primaryUi redirects to the chased player's combat, inventory and HUD state when a spectator has a chase target, and a test covers the chase HUD.

rows.title: Inspect clients and remove a player
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted e06b6ee joins local dedicated status, dumpuser and selected-player kick for classic and rerelease Q2. Complete native transport status columns, UDP kick-reason delivery and required wire/profile qualification remain open.
rows.currentReason: Local status prints only slot, score, ping and name and dumpuser works; kick now delivers its reason over UDP to peers, but the stock status columns (address, last message, qport) are absent and wire/profile qualification of the whole path is unverified.

rows.title: Discover servers from UDP, HTTP, and LAN sources
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: ServerBrowser discovery/state utilities are not constructed by the startup application, which lacks the required browser/favorite/status UI workflow.
rows.currentReason: StartupServerBrowser constructs a ServerBrowser per protocol including Q2 and is opened by startup, with master, LAN and favorite discovery sources.

rows.title: Filter and sort server results
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: ServerBrowser discovery/state utilities are not constructed by the startup application, which lacks the required browser/favorite/status UI workflow.
rows.currentReason: The browser supports text filter, favorites-only, hide empty and full, and ping, name, map and player-count sort orders.

rows.title: Inspect server rules and player details
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: ServerBrowser discovery/state utilities are not constructed by the startup application, which lacks the required browser/favorite/status UI workflow.
rows.currentReason: The browser details view lists server name, map, player count, per-player name, score and ping, and sorted server rules from the status response.

rows.title: Edit and persist ordered map rotations
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: LMCTF reads its maplist, but startup has no ordered rotation editor with persisted membership/shuffle and module-specific launch routing.

classification.note: Persisted rotation editing is assigned to server administration.

rows.currentReason: The in-game server settings menu has an ordered rotation editor (add, reorder, remove) with a rerelease shuffle toggle, backed by sv_maplist/g_map_list, saved in server profiles and consumed by the Q2 player module at map end.

rows.title: Choose maps and inspect mode eligibility
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Startup lists selected-product maps, but full Q2 spawn/objective-based mode eligibility filtering and authored map titles are not established by those choices.

classification.note: Map eligibility and selection are assigned to server setup.

rows.currentReason: Authored titles are shown for mapdb starts, but for Q2 (and Q3) maps the startup list accepts every BSP without checking spawn points or objectives; only Q1 maps are filtered by info_player classes, so mode eligibility filtering is missing.

rows.currentReason: The Q3 endpoint handles authenticated rcon through RconService, and the application joins operator filters, setmaster/heartbeat, kick/map/restart and G_LogPrintf logging to g_log with g_logSync.

rows.currentReason: The startup server browser joins LAN, primary and secondary master lists, and persisted favorites with refresh and a master-list fetch.

rows.title: Select base, expansion, CTF, LMCTF, and KEX game providers
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Known base/expansion/CTF/LMCTF/RR programs have real dispatch, but unknown native Q2 modules still lack executable guest application integration; rejecting them does not supply that component.
rows.currentReason: Base, expansion, CTF, LMCTF and rerelease programs dispatch to real providers, and unknown Q2 add-ons with a native game library run through the prepared native guest path.

rows.title: Mod discovery, selection and return to base
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Installed product selection is available, but arbitrary Q3 fs_game mod selection, restart and role/content reloading are not an implemented application workflow.
rows.currentReason: Q3 mod directories with vm/qagame.qvm are discovered as catalog products, selectable at startup and run as QVM guests; base product return is a normal selection. Live set fs_game plus restart is not supported (rejected at startup).

rows.title: QVM game, cgame and UI execution
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: QVM parsing/interpreting exists, but application game/cgame/UI roles execute native TypeScript controllers; loading and running the required bytecode roles is not joined.
rows.currentReason: Game, cgame and UI QVM roles all run: Q3QvmServerGame is built by the runtime and the q3 client creates QvmApplicationScalars, QvmCgame and QvmUi.

rows.title: Rerelease gib and corpse collision semantics
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted 98074c6 corrects native authored soldier/dog gib and head construction through existing helpers in source order; root passed 14 tests/301 assertions and actual rerelease head flight/persistence plus gib gravity/bounce/removal. Complete independently selected rerelease corpse-extension collision semantics remain unestablished.
rows.currentReason: Rerelease edition marks Q1 corpses as box solids with a corpse flag; traces hit them with point or zero-size shapes but never block sized bodies, and gib/head construction and bounce movement are in place.

rows.title: Match Q2 64 server movement and prediction
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted 3176aee joins selected Q2 movement profiles and source-announced server configuration, including actual authored bio/base travel; root passed 1 test/68 assertions. Rerelease remote-client admission and matching native prediction remain unsupported, so full Q2 64 server/client movement compatibility is not established.
rows.currentReason: The server publishes the n64 physics config and rerelease protocol admission is supported, and the remote client builds its prediction profile from the received n64 setting so native prediction matches.

rows.title: Bot combat, swimming, jumps and monster interactions
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared bots execute real movement and attacks, but Q1 admission rejects campaign play, leaving the required campaign-monster combat/traversal workflow unjoined.
rows.currentReason: The rerelease bot service drives real movement, combat and traversal in singleplayer, coop and deathmatch Q1 worlds; the legacy admission restriction applies only to the Q3-definition fallback.

rows.title: Bot objectives and campaign participation
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: botAdmissionError explicitly rejects Q1 team and campaign objectives, including CTF, coop and Horde.

classification.note: Bot participation requires mode-specific objective policies; its primary behavior is AI.

rows.currentReason: Rerelease bot objectives report Q1 CTF, coop and horde game types with team and flag-carrier hooks; the botAdmissionError rejection now applies only to classic-data legacy bots.

rows.title: Bot personalities, weapon/item knowledge and skill
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q1 maps currently load q3-baseq3 bot definitions in createBots rather than the active Q1 retail characters/knowledge/chats/team files.
rows.currentReason: Q1 maps load the rerelease Quake 1 bot knowledge, characters and localization (with sibling lookup of the installed rerelease product); baseq3 definitions are used only for Q3 maps or when no rerelease bot data is installed.

rows.title: Manual bots, autofill and eligibility
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared bot population is connected only for standard deathmatch on Q1 id1 and uses Q3 bot definitions; required native Q1 personality and broader mode population workflow remains unfinished.
rows.currentReason: Where Q1 rerelease bot definitions are installed, the native Q1 bot service handles manual and autofill bots without the id1-deathmatch limit; classic-only installs fall back to the restricted legacy policy (deathmatch, id1, no teamplay).

rows.title: Execute bot combat and campaign decisions
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared bots provide combat/item/movement decisions, but complete Q2 authored campaign objective solving is not established; the rerelease guidance hook still reports no-navigation.
rows.currentReason: Bots receive objective data for Q2 CTF, LMCTF, Tag, DeathBall and coop/campaign points of interest, and the rerelease guidance returns a path whenever native navigation is loaded.

rows.title: Update routes for doors, lifts, hazards, and moving floors
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted a5fca35 supplies live enabled, locked, destination and hazard observations to shared route validation. Unsupported mover travel is still rejected, so complete dynamic route execution remains unfinished.
rows.currentReason: Live door/plat enabled and locked state, destinations, hazard volumes, elevators and train routes feed route validation; only trains and nav-type-6 elevators get dedicated mover traversal, other moving-floor mover edges fall back to generic walk prediction and are rejected if not admitted. Full coverage of every mover type was not verified.

rows.title: Construct navigation for maps without NAV2
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Constructed graphs drive real foreign-map movement, combat and item access, but admitted shared bots exclude campaign/team objective play. The stated objective navigation component is not completed by the current application join.
rows.currentReason: Constructed graphs drive bot movement, combat and item access on maps without NAV2, and admitted bots now include the CTF, Tag, DeathBall and coop objective play via the shared objective binding.

rows.title: AAS reachability, clustering, writing and optimization
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Runtime AAS routing and generated common graphs exist; the distinct source AAS reachability/cluster generation, optimized AAS writer and read-back operation are not joined.
rows.currentReason: Ports of AAS reachability, clustering, optimization and writing exist and are round-trip tested, but nothing in the application calls them; navigation loads a shipped .aas/.nav or falls back to sampled construction.

rows.title: Navigation construction for foreign maps and moving geometry
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Foreign-map navigation construction supports ordinary play, but the application explicitly rejects foreign-map campaign/team objective bot policies; the complete required objective adaptation is missing.
rows.currentReason: Navigation is constructed for Q1, Q2 and Q3 worlds with a world adapter covering doors, plats, trains and hazards of each source; botAdmissionError no longer rejects foreign maps. Remaining objective-mode gaps belong to q3.modes.foreign-objective-adaptation.

rows.title: Hipnotic armagon encounter
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Native mission-pack actor behavior is registered, but the requirement also specifies foreign-map integration; the selectable Q1 monster catalog exposes only id1 ordinary species.
rows.currentReason: Native Armagon behavior is registered and offered as a selectable hipnotic monster; the expansion test places it as a replacement on a foreign map with save continuation. Authored bosses on foreign maps are deliberately kept map-defined.

rows.title: Hipnotic gremlin encounter
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Native mission-pack actor behavior is registered, but the requirement also specifies foreign-map integration; the selectable Q1 monster catalog exposes only id1 ordinary species.
rows.currentReason: Native Hipnotic gremlin behavior is registered, the monster catalog now offers it as a hipnotic/rogue-style source, and selected-monster admission includes monster_gremlin; tests place it on a foreign Q2 map and verify save continuation.

rows.title: Hipnotic scourge encounter
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Native mission-pack actor behavior is registered, but the requirement also specifies foreign-map integration; the selectable Q1 monster catalog exposes only id1 ordinary species.
rows.currentReason: Native Hipnotic scourge behavior is registered, the monster catalog now offers it as a hipnotic/rogue-style source, and selected-monster admission includes monster_scourge; tests place it on a foreign Q2 map and verify save continuation.

rows.title: Dawn of the Machine lava suit
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: item_artifact_lavasuit and its timed environmental immunity are absent from native MG3 pickup/player registration; the ordinary biosuit is not equivalent.
rows.currentReason: item_artifact_lavasuit is registered with a 30-second timed powerup, wearing-out warnings, HUD timer, save/restore, and lava/slime immunity in the damage path.

rows.title: Toggle power armor and consume cells on protection
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared screen/shield absorption, facing and cell accounting are joined, but the common Q2 HUD does not expose the required active power-armor indicator.
rows.currentReason: Toggle, absorption and cell accounting run, and the common HUD adds a prompt line showing active power screen or shield and remaining cells (text, not the original armor icon).

rows.title: Activate and expire invulnerability
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Protection, source damage flags and expiry run; the current common HUD omits the required invulnerability timer.
rows.currentReason: Invulnerability remaining time is in the Q2 powerup timer list and reaches the HUD timer renderer.

rows.title: Activate and extend quad damage
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source multiplier, durations, warning/drop behavior run, but the required active quad HUD timer is not populated by ApplicationSeatUi.
rows.currentReason: Quad Damage is included in the Q2 powerup timer list that ApplicationSeatUi passes to the HUD timer renderer.

rows.title: Complete the guardian encounter
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Boss source attacks/phases/death run, but authored healthbar events are not consumed by the application HUD.
rows.currentReason: Boss healthbar events are consumed by the per-seat HUD state (localized name, fraction, visibility) and drawn as HUD health bars.

rows.title: Use coop item instancing
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Per-player pickup eligibility and checkpoint data exist, but emitted item-visibility events have no application per-seat visibility consumer.
rows.currentReason: Item-visibility events are consumed by the rerelease presentation, and the presentation scene hides items per local seat using that state.

rows.title: Activate double damage
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Damage multiplier and source expiration/warnings run, but the required active HUD timer is absent.
rows.currentReason: Double Damage remaining time is in the Q2 powerup timer list and reaches the HUD timer renderer; multiplier and expiry live in the mission pack items.

rows.title: Activate quad fire
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The source cadence modifier and expiry are integrated; the required active HUD timer is absent from the common player HUD.
rows.currentReason: DualFire Damage remaining time is in the Q2 powerup timer list and reaches the HUD timer renderer; modifier and expiry live in the mission pack items.

rows.title: Preserve foreign entity classes, fields and target graphs
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Selected foreign creature admission covers bounded source rosters and rejects unsupported class/placement combinations; every required foreign expansion entity adapter is not provided.

classification.note: Foreign entity fields and target graphs span adapters and roster admission; assigned to authored map behavior.

rows.currentReason: Selected-monster admission only preserves ordinary authored classes and plain spawn flags; other authored classes or flags (bosses, dormant/triggered monsters) throw 'does not yet preserve authored obligations', and foreign spawn text with unimplemented classes throws rather than being carried through.

rows.title: Complete hubs, objectives, secrets, and endings
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Mission gates/targets run, but complete authored intermission/help statistics and Q2 cinematic ending/nextserver presentation are not joined.
rows.currentReason: End-of-unit reports list per-level kills and secrets, the help computer and objectives reach the HUD, and campaign cinematics plus nextserver travel are joined and exercised by a mixed-campaign test.

rows.title: Restore revisited levels within a unit
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: World travel constructs a fresh simulation and carries player/campaign state; there is no visited-level world checkpoint cache restoring killed monsters/movers/pickups on return.
rows.currentReason: CampaignUnit retains departed world bytes and restores them on revisit, and native classic and rerelease guests keep a visited-level map restored on return in single-player.

rows.title: Launch authored campaign starting maps
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Catalog start maps and skill are wired, but authored mapdb start-item/unit metadata is not loaded by the current catalog/application path.
rows.currentReason: Rerelease mapdb.json is parsed into ordered authored starts including start items; application launch loads them and applies the start items to the simulation.

rows.title: Resolve mapdb, maplist, and BSP start maps
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Current launch catalog has fixed product starts and BSP map discovery; no shared mapdb parser/caller preserves authored unit order and start items.

classification.note: Map metadata discovery serves campaign-start resolution.

rows.currentReason: The catalog loads mapdb.json through a shared parser that keeps authored unit order and start items, startup lists those starts first, and BSP discovery and the maplist file path cover the rest.

rows.title: Rerelease CTF capture, return, drop and scoring
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: CTF source capture/drop/return logic is installed, but its q1-composition ctf-status/capture events have no application HUD consumer.
rows.currentReason: CTF capture/drop/return logic is installed and its ctf-status and ctf-capture events are consumed by the seat HUD state (score, flag state, runes, capture banner).

rows.title: Rerelease CTF grappling, observers and exit vote
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Grapple and observer/vote source callbacks exist, but Q1 targeted prompt/choice events are not consumed by the application UI, leaving the complete observer/vote workflow unfinished.

classification.note: One retained row combines grapple, observer and voting requirements; it is not split or duplicated.

rows.currentReason: Observer team prompts and vote exits are consumed by the seat game-prompt menu which sends the chosen impulse; a first-playable test drives the team prompt, observer promotion and prompt clearing.

rows.title: Horde launch, wave spawning and survivor progression
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Native MG1 horde maps can schedule waves, but runtime omits the horde cvar so the manager cannot enable horde-dependent lifecycle/travel; dedicated launch controls and campaign/team bot admission are also missing.
rows.currentReason: Horde is a launch preset and --rules option; the runtime sets the horde cvar and adjoins the MG1 horde addon on any Q1 program, so waves, lifecycle and travel run on authored horde maps.

rows.title: Play rerelease DeathBall
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The source mode module exists, but application match construction selects only standard/CTF/LMCTF and startup exposes no actual Tag/DeathBall launch.
rows.currentReason: Match selection supports q2:deathball, startup builds DeathBall presets and accepts --rules deathball, and foreign-world DeathBall also runs in the runtime.

rows.title: End a deathmatch on authored limits
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source rules exist, but native application construction supplies deathmatchFlags=0/default player rules and does not bind the complete requested limit/option settings to gameplay.
rows.currentReason: Native Q2 deathmatch construction binds dmflags, timelimit and fraglimit cvars to the live rules, and the player module ends the match on time or frag limit.

rows.title: Apply classic deathmatch flags
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source rules exist, but native application construction supplies deathmatchFlags=0/default player rules and does not bind the complete requested limit/option settings to gameplay.
rows.currentReason: Native Q2 construction derives deathmatchFlags from dmflags (and rerelease g_dm_* cvars) and passes them to the game, with read/write service so in-game changes persist.

rows.title: Apply rerelease deathmatch and weapon settings
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source rules exist, but native application construction supplies deathmatchFlags=0/default player rules and does not bind the complete requested limit/option settings to gameplay.
rows.currentReason: Rerelease deathmatch and weapon cvars (instant switch, weapons stay, infinite ammo, no-items, force respawn, etc.) are registered, bound to rules and merged into dmflags at construction.

rows.title: Play Rogue Tag
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The source mode module exists, but application match construction selects only standard/CTF/LMCTF and startup exposes no actual Tag/DeathBall launch.
rows.currentReason: Match selection supports q2:tag, startup builds Tag presets and accepts --rules tag, and foreign-world Tag also runs in the runtime.

rows.title: Use squad respawn and cooperative lives
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Rerelease source implements squad/lives state, but application construction does not bind selectable rerelease coop options; complete configured waiting/restart workflow is not established.
rows.currentReason: Rerelease coop options (squad respawn, instanced items, lives, life count) are bound to g_coop_* cvars that feed the live rules object, and the player module runs the lives, waiting and coop respawn flow.

rows.title: Objective and spawn adaptation on foreign maps
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Foreign-map ordinary movement/combat/bots work, but the application explicitly lacks complete objective-anchor/campaign adaptation for all Q3/TA modes on Q1/Q2 maps.
rows.currentReason: Only Q2-style flag and team spawn classnames are translated to Q3 roles; the runtime never passes explicit objective placements, so 1FCTF, Overload and Harvester (and CTF on Q1 or flagless Q2 maps) fail with missing-objectives instead of being adapted.

rows.title: Single-player arena match flow
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The game-side single-player mode runs, but arena launch, progression completion and return-to-selection flow are not joined.
rows.currentReason: Base arena single-player flow is joined: catalog-driven selection with unlock gating, spmap launch at chosen skill, completion recording, and retry/next return paths in the application.

rows.title: Timed autosave and recovery
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Application consumes Q2 autosave events only; Q1 level-start/timed autosave scheduling and its multiplayer/seat policy are not joined.
rows.currentReason: Level-start autosave is joined for Q1 source worlds (singleplayer, sv_autosave), but the registered sv_autosave_interval cvar is never read, so no timed autosave exists, and multiplayer or seat policy is not addressed.

rows.title: Classic version 5 save import and export
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Classic save syntax exists, but application save/load is native SaveImage and does not import/export complete classic VM globals/edicts/callbacks; QC saved games remain rejected.
rows.currentReason: save <name> v5 exports and load imports the original NetQuake version 5 format for an idle singleplayer QuakeC source world; mixed compositions are refused with a message.

rows.title: KEX-style version 6 save compatibility
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: KEX container parsing is not an application retail-save import/export path; complete original fixture compatibility is not established.
rows.currentReason: save <name> v6 exports the KEX-style version 6 header with game directories, and load imports it through the same original-save path. Retail v6 fixtures are not in the tree, so compatibility rests on the format codec tests.

rows.title: Distinguish autosaves from transition snapshots
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Autosave events call the common saveGame path, but the full source distinction between transition snapshots and autosave-specific client/field treatment is not implemented.
rows.currentReason: Autosaves go through the common saveGame path (autosaveLevel, sv_autosave) but the native guest capture hard-codes autosave false for both rerelease and classic originals, so the source autosave flag and autosave-specific client treatment are never exercised; SavePurpose transition/autosave only gates eligibility.

rows.title: Enforce save eligibility and contained slot paths
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Startup slots are contained, but the live save command accepts an arbitrary path and lacks the full source eligibility/reserved-current-state policy.
rows.currentReason: The live save command resolves its name inside the save directory, saveGame applies saveUnavailable eligibility (no deathmatch, intermission, dead player or network authority) and writeContainedSave rejects escapes and the reserved current slot; `load` of a path outside the save directory is accepted only from the local console unless `--allow-load-paths` is given (assertLoadPathAllowed); tests/app/load-path-policy.test.ts covers these.

rows.title: Restore objective and presentation state
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source state is checkpointed and story redraws, but POI and healthbar application consumers are absent so those presentation components cannot resume visibly.
rows.currentReason: The rerelease module checkpoints story, POI, health bars and mission state, and restore re-emits sky, story, fog and POI presentation while health bars re-emit every player frame; a gameplay test covers resumePresentation.

rows.title: Complete unified world saves under Q3 gameplay
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Application/shared save still rejects complete Q3 world restoration; session carry does not save entities, missiles, timers, objectives and bot runtime state.
rows.currentReason: Q3 world saves capture q3:native game memory, world:q3-runtime (arsenals, movement, last attacks), bots and simulation state, with a restore path; a persistence test covers it. Tag/LMCTF/DeathBall foreign-match state on other families is still rejected, which is outside this row.

rows.title: Localized prompts and choice impulses
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source emits Q1 prompt/clear-prompt events, but Application.sourceActions and the seat UI do not construct/route those dialogs or selection impulses.

classification.note: Choice prompts include localized text; assigned to the interactive prompt workflow.

rows.currentReason: Q1 prompt and clear-prompt events are routed to a paged seat prompt menu that sends the chosen impulse.

rows.title: Classic, Hipnotic and Rogue HUD/inventory layouts
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Common health/armor/ammo and expansion weapon metadata are displayed, but Q1 CTF status/capture events are ignored, leaving required source scoreboard/objective HUD state incomplete.
rows.currentReason: The seat HUD state consumes Q1 ctf-status and ctf-capture events and shows team scores, flag state, runes and capture banners alongside health, armor, ammo and expansion weapons.

rows.title: Complete options, binding and reset workflows
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Current options cover a subset; language, sound rate, autosave, pickup switching, lookspring/lookstrafe and complete defaults controls are not all joined.
rows.currentReason: Settings cover language, output sample rate, autosave, pickup weapon switching, lookspring, lookstrafe and restore-defaults for settings and bindings.

rows.title: Rendered radial weapon selection
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: A working common radial selector is connected, but the required authored slot data is not: q1 wheel parsing/adaptation has no application caller and UI uses fixed source weapon-registration order.
rows.currentReason: The application reads the authored wwheel.txt for rerelease Q1 products, parses it, maps slot impulses to items and feeds the radial selector; invalid files fall back to the default wheel.

rows.title: Save, load and autosave selection UI
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Startup lists native saves and console save/load works, but complete in-game manual save-slot/comments menus and Q1 autosave recovery are absent.
rows.currentReason: In-game Save and Load menus with named slots and overwrite exist, startup lists native saves, and Q1 single-player level autosave (autosave.sav) is written on load; the timed autosave interval cvar has no reader.

rows.title: Weapon-wheel data and quickswitch impulses
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The common wheel selects source item IDs, but no application quickswitch/last-weapon eligibility path or authored Q1 wheel-slot/impulse cache adapter is connected.
rows.currentReason: An authored Q1 weapon wheel adapter maps wheel slots to exact source items and expansion impulses, and impulses 1-8, 10 and 12 plus weapnext/weapprev/use are wired through the application.

rows.title: Apply video, audio, and input settings
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted 0065d73b joins named/default audio-device selection and per-product device/effects/music persistence through ConfigStore; 36f395ee joins input assignment, tuning and binding persistence. Actual CPU/GL menu/restart and remote travel checks passed. The complete display/video settings and restart workflow remains unqualified.

classification.note: One row covers settings across several services; assigned to the public menu workflow.

rows.currentReason: Settings menus apply display (renderer, fullscreen, resolution, vsync, brightness), audio and input settings live, with ConfigStore persistence for audio and input; the old gap was a qualification status, not missing code. The GL restart test is gated behind QUAKE_GL_SMOKE.

rows.title: Display and clear authored boss health bars
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Rerelease emits objective/healthbar state, but ApplicationRereleasePresentation does not consume those events; the navigation hook explicitly returns no-navigation.
rows.currentReason: The rerelease module emits healthbar events every player frame (including a clearing event) and SeatSourceHud keeps them per slot and seat and draws them in the HUD.

rows.title: Queue localized centerprints and notifications
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Per-seat Unicode message drawing is joined, but Q2 application centerprints always use instant=true and do not carry required source typewriter/duration policy.
rows.currentReason: Per-seat localized centerprints and notifications are drawn, but no Q2 local emitter sets instant or durationSeconds, so local centerprints always fall to instant with a five second hold; the typewriter policy is only honoured on the network service path.

rows.title: Draw the compass route to the active objective
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Rerelease emits objective/healthbar state, but ApplicationRereleasePresentation does not consume those events; the navigation hook explicitly returns no-navigation.
rows.currentReason: help-path events are consumed by SeatSourceHud and drawn as the compass route in the common HUD, with source-time lifetime; navigation returns a path when native navigation exists.

rows.title: Display damage direction and pickup feedback
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source damage blend/kick exists, but full directional HUD indicators and actual pickup icons/timers are not bound in ApplicationSeatUi.
rows.currentReason: Directional damage indicators (with the pickup damage picture) and pickup icons with a three second timer are bound through SeatSourceHud into the HUD; damage blend and kick also exist.

rows.title: Open and use the inventory display
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The common HUD draws vitals and active weapon status, but does not bind the full Q2 inventory/help/status-layout stream required by this workflow.
rows.currentReason: svc_inventory is bound to the native inventory layout and to an inventory menu opened by the source inventory event, with selected-row and use bindings.

rows.title: Activate and advance objective markers
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Rerelease emits objective/healthbar state, but ApplicationRereleasePresentation does not consume those events; the navigation hook explicitly returns no-navigation.
rows.currentReason: SeatSourceHud consumes poi, keyed-poi and remove-poi events, loads their pictures and publishes them as source points; the module checkpoints poi stage state.

rows.title: Use powerups through the radial wheel
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Powerup selection is wired, but required consumable/timer feedback is not populated in the common HUD.
rows.currentReason: Powerup selection, counts and active timers work, but wheelIcons is filled only for weapon items, so powerup wheel entries have icon null and draw as text labels instead of item art.

rows.title: Select the correct classic or rerelease HUD
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The common HUD draws vitals and active weapon status, but does not bind the full Q2 inventory/help/status-layout stream required by this workflow.
rows.currentReason: The Q2 native HUD layout stream is driven by the protocol identity (classic vs rerelease/kex) and is prepared and drawn from the application presentation path; tests cover both grammars.

rows.title: Display scoreboards and the help computer
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The common HUD draws vitals and active weapon status, but does not bind the full Q2 inventory/help/status-layout stream required by this workflow.
rows.currentReason: Scoreboard rows, the help computer and end-of-unit report are consumed by SeatSourceHud and the native svc_layout path, and are drawn through the common and native HUD; tests cover both.

rows.title: Cycle weapons with the carousel
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Carousel state exists in SeatWeaponWheel, but application input does not call its cycle path, so the source-style preview/confirmation workflow is unjoined.
rows.currentReason: weapnext and weapprev call ApplicationSeatUi.cycleWeapon for the rerelease dialect, which drives SeatWeaponWheel.cycle with timed preview, attack confirmation and a weapon lock.

rows.title: Select a weapon with the radial wheel
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The actual radial wheel is joined to source selection, but ApplicationSeatUi still supplies icon:null for wheel items; required item icons are not finished.
rows.currentReason: The wheel is joined to source selection and ApplicationSeatUi now loads per-weapon icons into wheelIcons and passes them to wheel items.

rows.title: Podium, postgame and next-match navigation
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Native victory-pad entities exist; the ranked postgame UI, award sequence and progression return path remain unjoined.

classification.note: Postgame display/navigation crosses match progression; assigned to its public presentation workflow.

rows.currentReason: The spPostgame command is parsed into a podium, awards and unlocked-movie result, persisted, and shown by the base arena menu with retry/next/main controls; Team Arena postgame feeds the results menu with next/retry/quit.

rows.title: Demo, movie and configuration menus
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The application has no complete base demos/cinematics/config menu workflow; codec and console helpers alone do not provide these menus.

classification.note: Retained row explicitly requires menus over multiple services.

rows.currentReason: Startup menu exposes Demos, Movies and Configurations library menus backed by demo listing/playback, mounted video listing and config library services.

rows.title: Base hosting, browser and in-game menus
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source commands support many match operations, but the required host/browser/in-game menu workflows are not implemented by the common frontend.

classification.note: Host/browser behavior is represented here by its UI row; no backend row is duplicated.

rows.currentReason: Common frontend provides a Host a game menu, the shared server browser with favorites/sort/filter, and a Q3 in-game match menu (team, vote, callvote, addbot, kick). It is a common-frontend equivalent, not a port of the original ui.qvm layout.

rows.title: Base menus for player, controls and settings
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Common settings provide usable controls, but the full base source settings/player-model/configuration menu workflow and apply/restart behavior are not joined.
rows.currentReason: Common settings cover bindings, audio, video basics, accessibility and character model, but the Q3 setup menus (graphics quality, network rate, full player setup, apply/restart behavior) are not present in the common frontend; no r_picmip, rate or cl_maxpackets controls exist.

rows.title: Team Arena scripts, feeders and owner draws
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The legacy menu engine and mission HUD are joined, but the complete Team Arena front-end scripts/feeders, server refresh and mod/media application services are not.
rows.currentReason: The legacy menu runtime loads Team Arena scripts only for the mission HUD (ui/testhud.menu); the Team Arena front-end menus (ui/menus.txt, feeders, server refresh, mod/media services) are replaced by common frontend menus rather than executed.

rows.title: Team Arena skirmish launch and next match
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Team Arena skirmish selection, team/map/skill setup and its launch/return workflow are not joined to the frontend.

classification.note: Skirmish launch/next-match flow is a UI entry point with mode dependencies.

rows.currentReason: Team Arena skirmish levels 1-5 are built in startup selection (player/opponent teams, map, skill) and launched through the application; the results menu offers next, retry, demo and quit.

rows.title: Contrast and color-accessibility settings
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: High-contrast/reduced-flash toggles exist, but alternate typeface/color-accessibility controls and persisted application preferences are incomplete.
rows.currentReason: Settings expose high-contrast, reduced-flash, bold typeface and blue-yellow or monochrome color modes, persisted per seat through shared settings and applied to the HUD and menu fonts and skin colors.

rows.title: Timed subtitles and sound captions
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: CaptionTimeline has no application consumer; actual Q2 SRT resources also depend on currently unsupported OGV playback, and no authored Q1 sound-caption mapping was found.
rows.currentReason: Timed sidecar captions (SRT/VTT) are consumed by the seat HUD for sound voices and cinematics, selected by language; OGV playback exists. Q1 captions come from source-authored sidecars, not a separate mapping table.

rows.title: Localization, fallback and mod overlay precedence
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Localization supports overlays/formatting, but application Q1 messages are drawn raw and the active language selector is not bound; finales currently load English only.
rows.currentReason: Q1 messages are resolved through Q1MessageLocalization with ordered base, fallback and mod overlay tables, bound to the selected language; the finale shares the same instance, so it is not English-only.

rows.title: Complete readable non-color-only and caption workflows
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Caption data/scheduler and HUD support exist but no application media-event producer supplies timed captions; the common HUD initializes captions empty.
rows.currentReason: SeatSoundCaptions follows actual mixer voices and sidecars into the HUD captions list, and cinematic subtitles are produced by SeatMediaCaptions; color modes are non-color-only alternatives.

rows.title: Choose contrast backgrounds and alternate typefaces
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: High-contrast controls exist, but complete alternate-typeface selection plus persisted preferences is not provided by the current application.
rows.currentReason: High contrast, blue-yellow and monochrome color modes and a bold alternate typeface are settings bindings per seat, stored in archived cvars and applied to HUD and menu fonts; a test covers persistence.

rows.title: Scale menus, HUD, and console independently
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: HUD/text scale controls exist, but independent menu/HUD/console scale ownership on every actual draw path is not fully wired.
rows.currentReason: Per-seat archived hudScale, textScale and menuScale cvars feed the HUD, the in-game and startup menus, and the console uses its own archived con_scale.

rows.title: Display timed cinematic subtitles and captions
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared media decoders exist, but Q2 campaign/remote cinematic presentation and authored continuation are not joined; the only application cinematic owner is Q3 UI RoQ playback, with no Q2 timed subtitle producer.

classification.note: Cinematic scheduling is required, but the visible behavior is subtitles/captions.

rows.currentReason: Offline, remote and startup cinematics pass a SeatMediaCaptions producer into CampaignCinematic, which draws timed subtitle and sound captions over the picture using the seat's caption preference and language.

rows.title: Timed subtitles and captions for supplied media
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Caption data/settings helpers are present, but a complete source subtitle/caption event-to-visible-timeline application path is not established.

classification.note: Timed media dependency retained; assigned to caption behavior.

rows.currentReason: Screen cinematic captions and sound captions flow from caption data through SeatMediaCaptions to the seat UI captionCommands timeline renderer, gated by the captions preference.

rows.title: Readable UI, independent scales and accessibility
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Safe areas, HUD scaling and readable source fonts are implemented; the compound accessibility requirement including complete international text and caption presentation is not established in the actual application.
rows.currentReason: Per-seat HUD, text and menu scales, high contrast, colour modes, reduced flashes, captions toggle and language selection are archived cvar settings with a persistence test, and captions render through the seat UI.

rows.title: Bitmap, proportional and Team Arena glyph fonts
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Bitmap/proportional and DAT fonts are joined; the application constructs RendererFontRegistry without generation services, so the required configurable FreeType generation path remains unavailable.

classification.note: Glyph rendering and legibility share this font requirement.

rows.currentReason: The application constructs RendererFontRegistry with generation services (generated atlas registration, font-data saving, user-directory export), so the FreeType generation path is available alongside bitmap and DAT fonts.

rows.title: Achievement persistence and player UI
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Achievement events are emitted but there is no durable award store/provider identity or readable application achievement consumer.
rows.currentReason: Q1 achievement events are recorded in a durable player-progress store and shown through the Achievements and progress library menu.

rows.title: Level-completed events and return-to-lobby lifecycle
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Source completion/return events have no durable progression plus host/join/leave/start lobby lifecycle consumer.

classification.note: Level completion and lobby return share one row; assigned to external/session lifecycle.

rows.currentReason: Level-completed events are recorded as durable progress and application completion calls returnToLobby on the local lobby service, with host, join, leave and readiness handled by the lobby.

rows.title: Record authored achievement events durably
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The source emits achievement events, but no application achievement consumer provides durable per-participant recording/display.
rows.currentReason: Q1 and Q2 rerelease achievement events are recorded per participant in a durable PlayerProgressStore and shown in the player progress library.

rows.title: Complete match reporting and lobby lifecycle
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Local source match rules are implemented, but durable match-report and lobby membership/next-session service workflow is not integrated.
rows.currentReason: Q2 match reports are built and recorded durably at match end and the local lobby service handles return-to-lobby and next session.

rows.title: Difficulty-specific arena records
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The application has no joined five-skill best-rank progression store or record-driven arena UI.
rows.currentReason: BaseArenaProgression stores best rank per arena in g_spScores1 to g_spScores5 archive cvars and the selection menu shows the best rank and skill per arena.

rows.title: Persistent medals and award thresholds
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: In-match rewards exist, but durable single-player medal accumulation and its progression display are not joined.
rows.currentReason: Postgame results accumulate medal counts in the archived g_spAwards cvar with source thresholds, and the progress menu displays them.

rows.title: Progression reset and explicit unlock commands
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Progression reset/unlock commands do not have an application-owned progression record to update.
rows.currentReason: BaseArenaProgression owns the g_spScores/g_spAwards/g_spVideos archive cvars with reset, unlockLevels and unlockMedals; the application routes arena-reset, arena-unlock (iamacheater) and arena-medals to it and saves the source archive.

rows.title: Team Arena skirmish scores and best times
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Team Arena campaign score/accuracy/medal persistence and postgame record UI are not joined.
rows.currentReason: The Team Arena postgame command computes score, time and bonuses and writes the native games/<map>_<type>.game record on a new high score; ui_score cvars drive the results menu.

rows.title: Tier completion and movie unlocks
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Tier completion, video unlock and final/training progression rules are not joined to the common frontend.
rows.currentReason: Tier completion, training and final ordering, and movie unlocks via g_spVideos are implemented in BaseArenaProgression and driven by the application postgame hook.

rows.title: CD-key authorization and configurable service endpoints
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The actual Q3 admission adapter supplies authorizeAddress as null and immediately answers authorization challenges; the required authorization endpoint lifecycle is not joined.
rows.currentReason: Q3ServerAuthorization resolves authorize.quake3arena.com, caches the endpoint as authorizeAddress and sends getIpAuthorize with sv_strictAuth; IPX is excluded and a client-side authorization counterpart exists.

rows.title: Ranking login, match lifecycle and submission
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Ranking wire codecs exist without a joined ranking account/session/reporting lifecycle.
rows.currentReason: Rank wire codecs and an application q3-rankings.ts exist, but no ranking login, match-lifecycle or submission service was verified as joined to a real or configurable endpoint; not fully traced.

rows.title: NetQuake demo recording, playback and timedemo
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: NQ demo codec/recording library has no application record/playback/timedemo command and camera lifecycle join.
rows.currentReason: playdemo, timedemo, record, stop and rerecord are registered for .dem recordings, with local NetQuake recording and playback through the demo library.

rows.title: QuakeWorld demos, rerecord and spectator cameras
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted 66e6136 provides a live native QW remote session, but demo recording/playback/rerecord workflows and spectator cameras remain unjoined; spectator connections are rejected.
rows.currentReason: QuakeWorld .qwd record, playback and rerecord are joined through the demo commands, and the remote QW client has a spectator camera with teleport and chase tracking.

rows.title: Record and replay ordinary demos
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q2 demo/MVD codecs and stream utilities exist without a live application recorder/player/GTV service and corresponding user workflow.
rows.currentReason: The record and stop commands record Q2 client demos from a live Q2 source through ClientDemoRecording and the local recording feed.

rows.title: Authenticate and stream GTV spectators
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q2 demo/MVD codecs and stream utilities exist without a live application recorder/player/GTV service and corresponding user workflow.
rows.currentReason: mvdconnect and mvdisconnect authenticate to a GTV server and GtvRemoteSource streams MVD data into the remote application.

rows.title: Record multi-view demos
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q2 demo/MVD codecs and stream utilities exist without a live application recorder/player/GTV service and corresponding user workflow.
rows.currentReason: mvdrecord and mvdstop record the hosted Q2 world as a native multiview demo through the MVD recording feed.

rows.title: Play supported classic and rerelease demos
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q2 demo/MVD codecs and stream utilities exist without a live application recorder/player/GTV service and corresponding user workflow.
rows.currentReason: playdemo plays dm2 demos including KEX 2022 and 2023 headers, and MVD files, through Q2DemoPlayback into the remote application.

rows.title: Record server demos
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q2 demo/MVD codecs and stream utilities exist without a live application recorder/player/GTV service and corresponding user workflow.
rows.currentReason: serverrecord and serverstop record classic Q2 server entity footage from the hosted source.

rows.title: Control playback and recorded local viewpoints
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q2 demo/MVD codecs and stream utilities exist without a live application recorder/player/GTV service and corresponding user workflow.
rows.currentReason: Demo playback has demopause, follow and chase player selection for MVD and GTV, and recorded KEX viewpoints preserve per-seat identities.

rows.title: Demo recording and legacy playback
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Q3 demo codecs exist, but record/playback, snapshot consumption and demo UI/application lifecycle are not joined.
rows.currentReason: Q3 demos are recorded from a live local server (gamestate seed and snapshots) and played back through q3-demo/recorded-source via the demo command with clock handling.

rows.title: Timedemo clocks and performance reporting
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: There is no joined application timedemo command, playback clock and performance-result workflow.
rows.currentReason: Q3 uses the source timedemo cvar: RecordedRemoteSource honours it, the Q3 demo clock runs unthrottled, and end-of-demo timing is printed via demoTimingText. The timedemo command itself is registered only for Q1/QW, matching source.

rows.title: Decode and present classic CIN frames
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared media decoders exist, but Q2 campaign/remote cinematic presentation and authored continuation are not joined; the only application cinematic owner is Q3 UI RoQ playback, with no Q2 timed subtitle producer.
rows.currentReason: CampaignCinematic decodes and presents CIN (with OGV fallback), is used by the offline Q2 campaign, remote server requests and the startup frontend; a test plays, skips and completes unit CINs.

rows.title: Pause, skip, and finish cinematic transitions
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared media decoders exist, but Q2 campaign/remote cinematic presentation and authored continuation are not joined; the only application cinematic owner is Q3 UI RoQ playback, with no Q2 timed subtitle producer.
rows.currentReason: Cinematics pause (clock and audio), skip on input after one second and complete into the next travel target or quit via the movie completion hook; a test covers pause, skip, completion and failure fallthrough.

rows.title: Play required rerelease and expansion media formats
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared media decoders exist, but Q2 campaign/remote cinematic presentation and authored continuation are not joined; the only application cinematic owner is Q3 UI RoQ playback, with no Q2 timed subtitle producer.
rows.currentReason: The shared cinematic path plays CIN, RoQ and OGV (Ogg Vorbis/Theora demux) and falls back from .cin to .ogv for rerelease content; decoder tests cover all three.

rows.title: Present static PCX intermission images
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Shared media decoders exist, but Q2 campaign/remote cinematic presentation and authored continuation are not joined; the only application cinematic owner is Q3 UI RoQ playback, with no Q2 timed subtitle producer.
rows.currentReason: CampaignCinematic accepts .pcx names via cinematicPcx as held stills with skip, and the Q2 travel grammar routes picture destinations to it.

rows.title: Cinematic timing, looping, hold and skip
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Cgame cinematic slots play actual media, but the full standalone cinematic input/skip/end/nextmap transition workflow is not joined to Application.
rows.currentReason: The cinematic command opens a system cinematic with loop/hold/silent modes, skip and stop handles, and on completion queues the nextmap command and clears it.

rows.title: World material and menu cinematics
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Menu cinematic slots are joined, but ApplicationAssets constructs SceneShaderRegistry without playCinematic, leaving world videoMap stages unresolved. CinematicImage also rejects dimension changes instead of resizing the resource.
rows.currentReason: ApplicationAssets passes materialMovie as the SceneShaderRegistry cinematic provider so videoMap stages resolve, and CinematicImage reallocates on frame dimension change.

rows.title: Runtime chase camera and diagnostic commands
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Diagnostic console exists, but a player-visible traced Q1 chase-camera mode is not joined to the application view owner.
rows.currentReason: The presentation view owner applies a traced Q1 chase camera from the viewsize chase settings to the local view, and the chase cvars toggle it.

rows.title: Spline camera evaluation and timed camera events
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Runtime camera splines and their source-authored load/control/interpolation lifecycle are not joined to the application view.

classification.note: Spline evaluation and timed camera tooling depend on rendered camera presentation.

rows.currentReason: ApplicationSplineCamera registers load/save/control camera commands and its apply hook is passed into every WorldSeatPresentation view; tests cover spline evaluation and the workflow.

rows.title: OmniTimer initialization, stamps and reporting
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: The required OmniTimer runtime/profiling contract has no established application implementation.
rows.currentReason: OmniTimer is a core runtime profiler owned by ApplicationTools, with timers on/off/reset/report/stamps and timerstamp commands and async measurement hooks.

rows.title: Runtime diagnostic and developer commands
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Diagnostic primitives exist, but the complete source runtime diagnostic command set is not registered against the actual application owners.
rows.currentReason: ApplicationTools registers timers, timerstamp, meminfo, path, dir, touchFile, resourceinfo, frameinfo and renderer diagnostics (imagelist, shaderlist, modellist, skinlist, modelist, gfxinfo) against the live owners, alongside cmdlist/cvarlist/soundinfo/midiinfo. Exhaustive comparison with every source developer command was not done.

rows.title: Screenshots, levelshots and capture timing
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Accepted fc0c15e implements automatic/named/silent screenshot commands, TGA/PNG/JPEG output, source-style 128x128 levelshot downsampling and complete-frame readback through the shared application capture path. Recording capture-clock integration with FPS/timescale and restart/timing behavior remains unfinished; screenshot and levelshot helper absence is no longer the gap.

classification.note: Screenshot and levelshot capture belongs to tools, with rendered output and frame timing dependencies.

rows.currentReason: Screenshot/levelshot commands and formats ship, and capture frames are timed from cl_avidemo, timescale and cl_forceavidemo in both the local and remote applications.

rows.title: Separate authoring and distribution application roles
rows.originalRemainingWorkReason: Comparison documentation enumerates authoring/runtime roles, but complete runtime-derived obligations from all listed tool/SDK/archive inputs have not been established; this row cannot be completed from file inventory alone.
rows.currentReason: Remaining: no Quake III map compiler (q3map), QVM assembler (q3asm/lcc) or SDK/archive packer exists in the repository; the AAS compile role is tools/navigation/aas.ts and the runtime roles are implemented. Not started: a q3asm-compatible assembler would be a new tool.
